plainTranslation: Opposite tastes and values that attract. You're drawn to what you don't share. Failure mode: friction over whose way is right. Treat the difference as range, not a referendum.
policy: Governed by synastry-policy. Descriptive, not deterministic; intensity is never treated as obligation, safety concerns override astrology.
note: Imported from approved project marquee synastry aspect material. Source file was not copied into the repository.
summaryDeep:
You may have felt it the first time you saw how they spent their money, or how they spent a free day. Something in you went, that is not what I would do. One of you feels safest when there is something saved. The other feels most alive spending on the thing that makes life beautiful right now. One wants the life settled. The other wants room to keep changing their mind about what they want.

At first the difference can be part of the draw. This person reaches for things you would never have reached for, and being near that can feel like a window into another way to live. They can widen you. You start to notice pleasures you had written off, and to suspect that your own taste is less a law of nature and more a habit you inherited.

The harder part is the moment the difference stops feeling interesting and starts feeling like a verdict. What feels generous to you can look reckless to them. What feels responsible to them can feel joyless to you. Nobody says it directly. It comes out as a small face at the restaurant bill, a certain silence about the purchase, a sense that the other person is quietly grading how you live. Few things sting like feeling judged for what genuinely makes you happy.

This one needs you to say it out loud instead of letting it curdle. Tell them what the thing actually gives you. Ask them the same, and listen past the part you find baffling. You do not have to want the same life. You have to stop treating your own preferences as the obviously correct ones.
